evidence.changes: Revision: the defender nearest the landing point attacks the ball; the direct side midfielder further from the ball pre-positions near the target man during build-up while the nearer one stays short; under pressure in the own half a ground pass past two or more pressers to a free team-mate is preferred.

analysis.longPasses: Long balls are completed 51% (realistic). The count is high because the direct side makes 631 passes per match (real long-ball teams about 350-400; engine-wide pass volume is about 1.4x real, a league-calibration item for rulebook layer 8). As a share, long passes are 29% of passes; real direct teams are about 15-25%.
analysis.escapes: A press-breaking ground pass (past two or more pressers to a free team-mate) exists in 48% of pressed own-third decisions, but its average risk is 0.58 because pressers stand in the lanes; the press is doing its job, so the long-ball side rationally goes long. Raising escapes further would mean weakening the press or overriding risk.
analysis.secondBalls: Direct side now wins 69% of the next possession after a long ball (was 74%); real duels are nearer 50%.
